contributions.summary: DAEA model: equity as inverse Mahalanobis dispersion, dimensionally adaptive.
AMO: a UN agency that licenses mining and redistributes a share of benefits.
P&A model separates production gains from redistribution transfers.
Concrete recovery time: 27 years, GEI 74.67 at year 50.

dependency_graph.handoff: Development Index and GEI definition drive the mining simulation

assumptions.summary: Countries grow at a decreasing rate (diminishing marginal utility).
An international organization can regulate mining and all countries comply.
Only asteroid mining changes the natural development rate.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Panel of 35 countries, 2010-2020, all continents except Antarctica. Sources: UNdata, World Bank, BP energy review, OpenStreetMap.

models.summary: DEQ: EWM plus CVM development index, Mahalanobis DAEA equity index, GEI 66.80.
PAM: Ward clustering, production-allocation difference equation, 27-year recovery.

verification.summary: Lambda sensitivity: 1 percent change shifts GEI by about 0.1 percent. Shape of the curve unchanged.

results_trace.summary: GEI before mining = 66.80. Technology dimension least equitable.
GEI falls then rises. Baseline restored in 27 years. GEI = 74.67 at year 50.
Medium countries joining cuts recovery to 25 years (after 20) or 21.5 years (after 10).

writing_logic.summary: Abstract opens with a Kennedy quotation and a science-fiction epigraph.
Model requirements stated as four adjectives: Universal, Comprehensive, Reasonable, Robust.
Policy dilemma posed as two unacceptable extremes before the AMO compromise.
Policy split into mandatory and incentive lists, five items each.

language_observations.summary: Epigraph from Legend of the Galactic Heroes plus a Kennedy quotation before any model.
'Then we paint a picture of asteroid mining' — visual verb for scenario building.
Triple apposition: 'a source of wonder, a place for discovery, a realm for aspirations'.
'which we are not willing to accept' — first person stakes a position.
Dilemma framed as two if-clauses, both bad, before the proposed institution.
'This conclusion is consistent with our intuition' — appeals to intuition after the numbers.
'it lacks specificity in implementation' — concedes the treaty's authority while justifying new rules.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Equity defined as inverse dispersion in a metric space is an original framing.
Inventing a named institution (AMO) with an emblem makes the policy concrete.
A numeric recovery time (27 years) is more memorable than a qualitative claim.

weaknesses.summary: Composite equity score hides the structure across dimensions.
Mining effects applied to superior indicators, not inferior ones.
Second-order difference equation may deviate from reality.

independent_extensions.summary: Apply mining shocks to the 12 inferior indicators directly.
Replace the difference equation with a Markov chain.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Dispersion-based equity index is reusable for any multi-entity fairness problem.
Mandatory-plus-incentive policy split balances enforcement and participation.

unresolved_questions.question: How are the beta coefficients in the dispersion score chosen?
What percentage of benefits do mining countries surrender?
